# `m.partners.fable.merchant_aggregates`

<!-- Generated by `uv run python scripts/render_reference.py`; do not edit by hand. -->

Daily European consumer spending per merchant, from Fable Data's transaction panel.

```python
m.partners.fable.merchant_aggregates(*, start=None, end=None, sort=None, order=None, limit=None, filters=None)
```

## Arguments

What each argument does for this dataset, and the rule it follows for every dataset that takes it.

| Argument | For this dataset | For every dataset |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `start` | The first transaction day. | The first day or moment of the range. A date (text such as `"2025-06-02"`, a Python `date`, or a Deephaven `LocalDate`) means the day in the market's time zone: New York for stocks, options, and indices; UTC for forex and crypto; for futures, the trading session that ends that day. An instant is an exact time: a Python `datetime` with a time zone, a `pandas.Timestamp`, a `numpy.datetime64`, a Deephaven `Instant` or `ZonedDateTime`, or Deephaven time text such as `"2025-06-02T09:30 ET"`. Give `start` and `end` as two dates or two instants. A `datetime` without a time zone raises `ValueError`, and a calendar-date field, such as an ex-dividend date, takes dates only. |
| `end` | The last transaction day. | The last day, or the moment the range stops, in the same form as `start`. A date includes its whole day, so `start="2025-06-02", end="2025-06-02"` reads all of June 2; an instant is excluded. Leave it out to read through now; a list dataset then sends Massive no end, so it also returns records still to come, such as dividends announced but not yet paid. |
| `sort` | Any field of the rows, such as `"transaction_date"`. | The field to order the rows by, named as Massive names it, such as `"ex_dividend_date"`. Where the endpoint allows, name several, separated by commas, each with an optional `.asc` or `.desc`: `"ticker,ex_dividend_date.desc"`. This page lists the values the dataset takes. |
| `order` | The direction of `sort`. | The direction of `sort`: `dm.Order.ASC` or `dm.Order.DESC`. |
| `limit` | The most rows to return, in total. | The most rows Massive returns for the whole request, across every symbol you name, kept in Massive's order: ask for newest first (`order=dm.Order.DESC`) to keep the latest. A symbol that comes first can use up the whole limit, so leave `limit` out when you need every row of each symbol. A `fetch()` that follows a table of symbols applies it to each symbol's request, and this dataset's own line says where else it applies to each symbol. |
| `filters` | Further endpoint parameters, such as `{"parent_name": "Amazon Inc"}`. | Any other parameter Massive documents for this dataset, as a mapping from the parameter's name to its value, with each dot in the name written as `_`: Massive's `strike_price.gte` is `strike_price_gte`. This page lists the keys the dataset takes. A key it doesn't take, or one that has its own argument, such as `start`, raises `ValueError` naming the keys it does take. A date or time value takes ISO 8601 text, or any value `start` takes. |

## Plan access

Which of Massive's plans include this dataset, how recent its data is on each, and how far back its history goes, as Massive's pages state them.

| Plan | Merchant Aggregates (REST) |
| --- | --- |
| European Consumer Spending by Merchant | 30-day delayed, All history |
| European Consumer Spending by Merchant Business | 7-day delayed, All history |

## Columns

| Column | Deephaven type | Description | Supplied by |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `Channel` | String | Transaction channel. Possible values: online, offline, bnpl (buy now pay later platforms such as Scala, Klarna, Zilch). | REST |
| `ConsumerType` | String | The panel the account is sourced from. Possible values: consumer_credit, consumer_debit, open_banking. | REST |
| `EightDayRollingCategoryAccounts` | long | The count of unique consumer accounts active for a given country, consumer type, and that transacted in this merchant category (MCC Group) over the prior 8 days. Used for short-term normalization calculations (e.g., spend per 1000 panelists = (total_spend / eight_day_rolling_category_accounts) * 1000). | REST |
| `EightDayRollingTotalAccounts` | long | The count of unique consumer accounts active for a given country and consumer type that had any transaction activity (across all categories) over the prior 8 days. Provides a baseline for total panel size. | REST |
| `MccGroup` | String | Merchant category code group associated with the merchant or payment processor. | REST |
| `MerchantIndustry` | String | Industry name based on GICS/BICS/ICB data classification for the merchant. | REST |
| `MerchantTicker` | String | Stock ticker associated with the merchant (~250 US public companies mapped). Uses Bloomberg tickers and they are point in time. | REST |
| `Name` | String | The merchant or entity name for this aggregate (lowercase). When type is 'merchant', this value can be used as the lookup_name in the merchant-hierarchy endpoint to retrieve full corporate hierarchy details. | REST |
| `ParentName` | String | Merchant's parent business name (Title Case). Useful for aggregating transactions across subsidiary brands. Also available in the merchant-hierarchy endpoint for full corporate structure. | REST |
| `PublishedDate` | String | The date when this data version was published. For original data, this is approximately 7 days after transaction_date. | REST |
| `SpendInDistinctAccountKeyCount` | long | The count of distinct account keys (unique consumer accounts) with inbound transactions. | REST |
| `SpendInSpend` | double | The total inbound transaction amount (refunds, returns, credits) in the specified currency for this aggregation. Values are positive, representing money flowing back into consumer accounts. | REST |
| `SpendInTransactionCount` | long | The count of inbound transactions (refunds, returns). | REST |
| `SpendOutDistinctAccountKeyCount` | long | The count of distinct account keys (unique consumer accounts) with outbound transactions. | REST |
| `SpendOutSpend` | double | The total outbound transaction amount (money spent by consumers) in the specified currency for this aggregation. Values are negative, representing money flowing out of consumer accounts. | REST |
| `SpendOutTransactionCount` | long | The count of outbound transactions (purchases, payments). | REST |
| `TotalAccounts` | long | The total count of distinct consumer accounts with any transaction activity for this aggregation. | REST |
| `TotalSpend` | double | Sum of spend_out_spend and spend_in_spend. Typically negative (net outflow). A positive value indicates refunds exceeded new spending for this aggregation. | REST |
| `TotalTransactions` | long | The total count of all transactions (outbound + inbound). | REST |
| `TransactionCurrency` | String | ISO currency code for the transaction (base card/account currency). Always EUR or GBP in this dataset. All spend amounts are denominated in this currency. | REST |
| `TransactionDate` | String | The calendar date when the consumer transactions occurred. | REST |
| `TwentyEightDayRollingCategoryAccounts` | long | The count of unique consumer accounts active for a given country, consumer type, and that transacted in this merchant category (MCC Group) over the prior 28 days. Used for longer-term normalization calculations. | REST |
| `TwentyEightDayRollingTotalAccounts` | long | The count of unique consumer accounts active for a given country and consumer type that had any transaction activity (across all categories) over the prior 28 days. Provides a longer-term baseline for total panel size. | REST |
| `Type` | String | The type of aggregation. Can be 'merchant' or 'payment_processor'. | REST |
| `UserCountry` | String | Country of consumer's residence (ISO codes). Available countries: UK, DE, FR, ES, IT, AT. Values outside these are mapped to 'unknown'. | REST |
| `TimestampInsert` | Instant | When the library received the row, as an Instant: the local clock when the REST page, flat-file block, or WebSocket frame that carried it arrived, the same for every row of one. It is not monotonic and is not Massive's own receive time; on history() rows it is the download time, and in a poll() table the latest poll's. | REST |
